concepts:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a high-fidelity design exploration board for "Still Brook", an independent blog about software, systems, and the craft of building. The chosen direction is an illustrated field journal: warm, odd, tactile, sophisticated, playful in small moments. Show TWO polished desktop homepage designs side-by-side, each about 700px wide and tall enough to see the first essay rows, on a neutral background. This is a web design flat screenshot, not a photograph of screens, no browser chrome. Both should feel like something a software craftsperson with a love of unusual machines would actually publish.

Direction A, on the left: warm ivory paper #f3f0e6, near-black charcoal ink, restrained rust-red accents. Very large elegant serif "Still Brook." masthead beneath a minimal top line of navigation "Essays / Field notes / About". Small descriptive copy "Notes on software & the things we make." A charming hand-inked woodcut illustration of a tiny impossible computer with branching wires beside a brook, like a naturalist's study of a new species of machine. Wide spacious editorial composition, excellent alignment, thin black rules, small monospaced index labels. Below, a two-column latest essay feature with title "The cabinet of impossible machines", followed by airy list rows of essays: "The type between the fields", "The button in the painting", "Camera control costs a thumb". Small line-art specimens sit in the margins, content stays clear.

Direction B, on the right: same warm field-journal spirit but a bolder asymmetric layout. A small "Still Brook" wordmark in top navigation, an immense serif headline "A few things, carefully considered." beside a large surreal engraved machine specimen, burnt-orange side tab, fine ruled paper details, essay index below. Use the same real essay titles. Do not use rounded cards, gradients, SaaS buttons, fake statistics or long marketing text. Organic found-paper character with meticulous modern web layout. This is a concept exploration; readable typesetting and strong visual hierarchy matter. Only imagery created here is decorative concept art, not actual article hero photos.
illustration:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create a standalone editorial illustration for the homepage masthead of "Still Brook", a field journal about software and the things people make. This is DECORATIVE SITE ART, not an article hero. No words, letters, numbers, captions, border, logo, or typography anywhere.
Subject: a curious impossible machine discovered beside a little brook. A compact 1980s personal computer with a small dark CRT screen sits on four thin wooden legs, like a naturalist's field instrument. Its open wooden side reveals a handful of lovely little gears, tiny spools and winding copper wires. From its top a delicate twig with three leaves grows; a long paper tape unspools, curling over a rock toward the brook. One tiny bird perches on the computer's top corner. The machine has a slightly funny dignified character, but no anthropomorphic face. Minimal setting: a few pebbles, thin grasses, three flowing lines of water. Most space remains empty.
Style: finely observed hand-inked copperplate engraving crossed with a thoughtful contemporary book illustration. Detailed but airy crosshatching, hand-wobbled dark charcoal strokes, very restrained rusty terracotta accents on a few small machine parts. Warm ivory untextured background #f3f0e6, near-black #302c25 ink. No solid color panel behind the subject. Full subject visible, landscape 3:2 composition, machine occupies central 65%, generous clear space around it. Tactile, quietly odd, adult, charming, never glossy, no digital gradients, no 3D rendering, no modern vector clip-art. The art must reproduce well at 500px wide in an elegant editorial website.
